heard: A new asteroid held a terrifying 3.1% chance of hitting Earth. On December 27, 2024, the Atlas Telescope in Chile spotted asteroid 2024 YR4 sneaking past a solar blind spot. The city killer reached level 3 on the Torino scale, the highest impact probability ever recorded for its size. Roughly 53 to 67 meters wide, it packed the explosive punch of 8 megatons of TNT. Its potential impact corridor stretched across parts of South America, India, and Nigeria. Then, James Webb Space Telescope observations ruled out Earth, leaving a 4% chance of hitting the Moon. Refined 2026, data finally cleared the asteroid entirely, ending the most threatening impact scare in history. That is how a new space rock briefly held a terrifying 3.1% chance of hitting Earth.
